verdict.rationale: Obsidian's core app runs entirely on the user's own device. Notes are plain Markdown files stored locally, it works offline, and it needs no sign-up, so the core product has no dependency on vendor servers [obsidian-docs-2, obsidian-docs-20, obsidian-docs-53]. Users can also replace the vendor's sync with their own Git, Dropbox or other storage [obsidian-docs-19, obsidian-docs-38], and a community user confirms notes are kept only on their own machine [obsidian-comm-9]. The vendor's own add-ons are cloud-only: Obsidian Publish is hosted at publish.obsidian.md, and Sync runs through Obsidian's servers [obsidian-docs-22, obsidian-docs-9]. Missing for 10: a self-hostable Sync/Publish server, evidence the core is open source or deployable on your own server, and independent hands-on corroboration of self-hosted setups.
